Recommended Intervention:
Install a three-arm differential manifold with a witness-ratio guard on the 40,000 m3/day SWRO train. This design restores Rank-2 Fisher observability, allowing the system to distinguish reference-arm contamination from test-arm biofilm fouling. The system triggers fail-closed abstention or automated alerts based on a witness-ratio threshold, eliminating the need for periodic blind chemical cleaning while maintaining precise intervention timing.

PARAMETER: Witness-ratio guard threshold — 0.03 — ASSUMPTION (value not stated in the cited record)
PARAMETER: Manifold configuration — Three-arm differential — EVIDENCE-BACKED [doi:10.5281/zenodo.24324955]
PARAMETER: Target estimation error reduction — 7.72% — EVIDENCE-BACKED [doi:10.5281/zenodo.24324955]
PARAMETER: Baseline estimation error (2-arm) — 71.17% — EVIDENCE-BACKED [doi:10.5281/zenodo.24324955]
PARAMETER: Reference contamination trigger level — 10% partial fouling — EVIDENCE-BACKED [doi:10.5281/zenodo.24324955]

Expected Measurable Effect:
The system cuts estimation error from 71.17% to 7.72% [doi:10.5281/zenodo.24324955]. This accuracy allows the control logic to separate reversible concentration polarization from irreversible biofilm fouling. Consequently, the plant can extend the cleaning interval from the forced 3-week CIP cycle back toward the designed quarterly interval by intervening only when true biofouling is confirmed, rather than reacting to sensor artifacts or reference-channel contamination.

Constraint Compliance:
C1 & C2 (No chlorine): The intervention is a diagnostic manifold change; it does not introduce chlorine-based disinfection, preserving polyamide membrane integrity.
C3 (Same permeate recovery): The manifold monitors differential pressure and flux signals to adjust cleaning timing; it does not alter hydraulic configuration or membrane area, thus holding permeate recovery constant as designed.
C4 (40,000 m3/day device): The three-arm manifold is scaled to the flow rates of a 40,000 m3/day train, with arms sized to maintain laminar-to-turbulent transition characteristics consistent with standard RO differential cartridges.

Falsification Test:
Protocol: Introduce a controlled 10% partial fouling agent (e.g., alginate gel) into the reference arm only.
Temperature: 25 C ambient operating temperature.
Duration: 14 days continuous monitoring.
Sample size n: 3 independent SWRO trains of similar capacity.
Pass Criteria: The system must identify reference contamination with an estimation error < 10% (specifically, not exceeding the 7.72% target mean) and trigger the witness-ratio guard ($\tau_{ref} > 0.03$) without false positives on clean reference arms.
Fail Criteria: If the system does not trigger the guard or maintains an estimation error > 20%, the observability claim is falsified.

Evidence Support:
The core mechanism of three-arm differential observability and the specific 71.17% to 7.72% error reduction is directly supported by [doi:10.5281/zenodo.24324955]. This study explicitly details the structural vulnerability of 2-arm systems and the solution provided by the 3-arm configuration with zero-oracle fail-closed abstention.
